column17: This FINDS a defect; it does not correct one, and the correction is not a relabel. The district raster is built inside the province raster, so a station's province and its district are one decision, and the nine-year products assert ADM1 == ADM2 + outside + unallocated: moving a province label alone would break that identity. Nor would a finer grid settle it - for four of the seven the simplified ADM2 polygons disagree with the curated record too (Hub Power falls in Karachi, both Guddu units in Dera Ghazi Khan, Tapal Energy in Lasbela), so the error is in the boundary geometry at these sites and not only in its rasterisation. What this cannot say is how much EMISSION moves, because the cube's weights are per-fuel pools rather than per-station mass; the generation share is an exposure measure, not a delta. Quantifying the delta requires the re-base itself. tests/test_power_province_boundary.py holds the list at seven so an eighth cannot appear in silence

Synthetic fertiliser nitrogen 3,775,000 against 3,808,775 t N (0.9 percent); the six shared livestock species 2.311 against 2.289 billion head (0.9 percent), with this inventory counting 1.36x FAOSTAT's sheep, 1.30x its camels and 1.10x its goats. column17: CANNOT localise the remaining 18.09 Mt, and does not try. Only the SUM of FAOSTAT's four managed-soils items is held, so attributing the residual to a pool would be a guess; what is established is that it is neither the nitrogen nor the direct-EF vintage, which leaves the indirect factors and the partition of 7.7834 Mt of excreted nitrogen. Pricing FAOSTAT items 5061-5064 separately is a public acquisition and would localise it. NOTE ALSO that this CORRECTED the manuscript rather than confirming it: Section 10 had attributed the difference to FAOSTAT's synthetic-fertiliser treatment, which is the one flow that agrees

column6: Pakistan's First Biennial Transparency Report (2024), national inventory for 2020-21, read against FY2020-21. The only comparator in this release matched on BOTH axes: the BTR states its own convention ("the fiscal year 1993-94 (referred to as 1994)", "Pakistan's 2020-21 inventory (referred to as 2021)"), so its year is a Pakistani fiscal year, and it reports on AR5 GWPs
column8: 28 crosswalk entries with declared tiers, not a code join: the two accounts SWAP rice cultivation and managed soils (the BTR books rice at 3.D and soils at 3.C), so a code-keyed comparison silently reads each against the other
column9: substantial and unquantified. Both accounts are built from Pakistani statistics - HDIP/OCAC energy, PBS production, the livestock census - so agreement on an activity-driven category is not independent confirmation of the activity. What differs is method, factors and completeness
column16: ratio per crosswalk entry where the tier admits one, plus two totals: excluding LULUCF, and restricted to categories both accounts estimate
column17: the headline national ratio is the LEAST informative number here. It averages category ratios spanning more than an order of magnitude, and the two accounts share their upstream statistics, so it is not an accuracy score. What the comparison does support is the decomposition: restricted to categories both estimate the totals agree far more closely, so most of the national difference is COMPLETENESS rather than estimation, and the seven categories concerned are the same rows pakemis_completeness_mass.csv carries without a bound. Two apparent order-of-magnitude disagreements (landfill and open burning) are one fate-split disagreement and neither ratio should be quoted alone

column6: Finance Division Statistical Supplement Table 14.3 'Commercial energy supplies' (coal imports + production, the national supply) and Table 14.1(4) 'Coal' Power column, against NEPRA SoIR Table 3 fuel energy in TOE and Table 17 coal net generation; IPCC 2006 Vol.2 Ch.1 Table 1.2 net calorific values for the rank blend

column8: the national public-power coal energy booked at 1.A.1.a, tested as a published energy against (a) the coal physically supplied to Pakistan that year and (b) the electricity NEPRA itself reports having generated from coal
column9: NEPRA Table 3 names the HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook as its source and HDIP's power tonnage is the consumption column of the same supply table, so the energy under test and that mass account are NOT independent of each other - which is the finding, not a limitation. The SUPPLY side is a different ministry's table, cross-validated cell-for-cell against the PBS extraction series (19,260 against 19,259 kt in FY2023-24). The GENERATION side (Table 17) shares no input with the energy side, which is why the nine-year efficiency row is the independent test
column16: the FY2023-24 supply bound survives all six rescue bases: Table 3's energy needs 29,531 kt at the fleet's rank composition against 24,719 kt supplied (119.5 percent). Rescue would need a stock drawdown of 42 percent of a year's national supply, or a lignite share of 41.6 percent where NEPRA prints 92.0 per station. Table 3's TOE per tonne of HDIP tonnage is ONE constant over six consecutive years to 0.016 percent. The mass-free implied efficiency is outside 28-47 in five of seven material years and swings 38.5 points
column17: This REFUTES the published control; it does not select a replacement and it moves no pin. Two of the four candidate accounts sit inside the band, so the audit narrows the field without choosing one. The Table 21 route's in-band efficiency is NOT independent corroboration of that route: it is generation divided by the energy the route itself constructs, which this file proves as an identity year by year. FY2015-16 and FY2016-17 carry too little coal generation (148 and 997 GWh) for the ratio to be interpretable and are excluded from the refutation count, not counted in its favour

column6: NEPRA State of Industry Reports 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 - per-station and GENCO coal tables - against HDIP's power-sector coal column (Finance Division Statistical Supplement Table 14.1(4)) and against NEPRA SoIR Table 3's published coal energy
column8: the national public-power coal lane, per plant-year: mass, rank, net generation and the energy they imply at IPCC rank-default calorific values
column9: the station masses and the generation come from the SAME regulator and often the same table, so the plant rows are NOT independent of each other - what is independent is the three-way comparison: the stations' own reporting, HDIP's apparent-consumption column (a different ministry, a different method) and Table 3's energy, which is HDIP's tonnage times a conversion. Two of the three share a tonnage, and the file says so rather than treating them as three votes
column16: closes on printed coal generation in all nine years. HDIP's tonnage CROSSES the station band - above it in FY2015-16, FY2016-17 and FY2021-22 to FY2023-24, inside in FY2017-18, below in FY2018-19 to FY2020-21. Table 3's published energy implies 322 kt in FY2015-16 rising to 29,528 kt in FY2023-24, the latter against a national supply of 24,719 kt
column17: this RECONCILES and does not re-base; selecting a reference series is a declared pin re-base. Four plant-years carry a reconstructed mass with an interval and no point, because no edition prints one: the imported lane while Sahiwal and Port Qasim commissioned, and two residuals whose burning station had not reached COD and whose RANK is therefore unknown, so their band spans lignite to imported and is correspondingly wide. An interval here is evidence of what is not known, not a estimate to be read at its midpoint
